There is an exception to the possessive rule where a word ends with an s. You just put an apostrophe after the s and all is good. English is weird.

Read your own link ;)

The general rule is that the possessive of a singular noun is formed by adding an apostrophe and s, whether the singular noun ends in s or not.

Lucas is a singular noun that ends in an "s". This means that to make it plural you add the apostrophe and the s - "Lucas's".

Exceptions to the general rule

Use only an apostrophe for places or names that are singular but have a final word in plural form and ending with an s.

The exception only applies when you are using a noun that consists of multiple words. One of the examples in your link, "Beverly Hills," is an exception because it's more than one word.
